title: What the implementer did with the spec it was given
description: The round's account of its own work. A round that records none, and a round that records unfinished work, both stop the pull request for a person to read — so an honest `unfinished` costs nothing that silence does not cost too.

status.description: complete only when you finished everything this dispatch handed you and `unfinished` is empty; unfinished otherwise. It is about the work you were given — a spec, a findings record, or a failing check — and never about anything you were not given: a fixer handed findings or a failing check answers for those and says nothing about a spec it never had. Claiming complete for work you did not finish is worse than saying unfinished, because the run stops for a person either way and only one of the two tells them the truth.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what you changed, written for the person deciding whether this may merge.

unfinished.description: Every part of the work you were given and did not do, with the reason — including work you were told to do and could not: a file the spec names that does not exist, two statements that contradict, a repair that is a decision for a person. An empty array when nothing was left. A fixer reports here on the findings or the failing check it was handed, never on a spec it was not given.

part.description: Which part of the work this is, named the way the thing you were given names it.

reason.description: Why it was left undone, in a sentence a person can act on.

reachability.description: Whether the spec's manual-testing marking is right for what you actually built. The marking is `user_visible` in the spec's front matter: true means the spec stops for a person to try it before it merges, because once it merges a person can see or do something new; false means it merges on its checks. Correct it only when you are certain, in either direction, and otherwise make no claim: the plan's marking then stands. Every other reason a pull request waits is untouched by what you say here.

claim.description: none makes no claim, and is the answer whenever you are not certain, whichever way the marking points. not-reachable-yet is only for a spec marked user_visible: true, and only when you are certain no person can reach anything it adds once it merges: nothing calls it yet, or its only way in comes from a later spec. Reachable means any way in at all: a typed command flag, a setting someone can turn on and a changed default can all be tried today, so "it is behind a flag" and "it is off by default" are never reasons for not-reachable-yet. reachable-now is only for a spec marked user_visible: false, and only when you are certain a person can see or do something new the moment it merges, by any way in at all — including a flag, a setting or a changed default. A claim that agrees with the marking changes nothing.

reason.description: One line a person will read in the pull request and in the run's report, quoted as your words: what can or cannot be reached once this merges, and how. An empty string with none. A claim with an empty reason is ignored.
